hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Select k disjoint subarrays with alternating signed weights from k down to 1.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Dynamic programming tracks the number of chosen subarrays and whether the current subarray is continuing.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Compute weight w = (k - j + 1) * (1 if j is odd else -1). Maintain dp[j][0] (closed) and dp[j][1] (open) transitions.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumStrength(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        dp = [[-float('inf')] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
        dp[0][0] = 0
        for j in range(1, k + 1):
            w = (k - j + 1) if j % 2 == 1 else -(k - j + 1)
            mx = -float('inf')
            for i in range(j, n + 1):
                mx = max(mx, dp[i - 1][j - 1])
                val = w * nums[i - 1]
                dp[i][j] = val + max(dp[i - 1][j], mx)
        ans = -float('inf')
        for i in range(k, n + 1):
            ans = max(ans, dp[i][k])
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: State transitions with running prefix maximum.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all combinations of k disjoint subarrays is exponential.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use dynamic programming with state open/closed to achieve O(n * k).
